note: Availability is not permission. A repository being public, or a dataset appearing on GitHub, says nothing about whether its contents may be used to train a model. This policy is applied per source and a source with no recognised licence is refused, not merely annotated.

allow.CC-BY-SA-4.0: attribution and share-alike; share-alike applies to the data, record it
allow.ODbL-1.0: attribution and share-alike on derived databases

review.GPL-3.0: copyleft: fine to train on, but the licence question for model weights is unsettled. Do not mix into a corpus that will be redistributed without a decision.
review.AGPL-3.0: as GPL-3.0, with the network clause
review.CC-BY-NC-4.0: non-commercial only: unusable if the model is ever sold or used commercially

deny.NONE: no licence stated: default copyright applies, training is not permitted
deny.RESEARCH-ONLY: research-only terms exclude model training for release
deny.CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0: non-commercial AND no-derivatives. A trained model is arguably a derivative and commercial use is excluded, so this cannot be used for training at all.
deny.CC-BY-ND-4.0: no derivatives: a trained model is arguably a derivative

rules: A source with no licence field is denied. Absence is not permission.
A public repository is not an open licence. GitHub availability proves nothing.
Every kept record carries its source id, licence, attribution string and shard checksum.
Review-licensed sources are held out of the main corpus until a decision is recorded.
Attribution strings are preserved verbatim, including required notice text.
